title: SAM Tensor Format (STF) — format-agnostic model weights on bare metal
goals: Define SAM Tensor Format (STF) — kernel-native, format-agnostic (stf.h)
Write tools/to_stf.py — universal host-side converter (GGUF, SafeTensors, synthetic)
Expand AI domain to 256 MiB for KV cache headroom
Wire STF loader into kernel_main — parse, index, dequantize on bare metal
Zero-warning clean build, Sprint 9 PASS on real hardware

results.final_verdict: Sprint 9 PASS -- STF weights live on bare metal

files_changed: kernel/main.c       — Sprint 9 banner, 256 MiB AI domain, STF loader section
kernel/stf.h        — NEW: SAM Tensor Format v1 (220 lines, static inline, no libc)
kernel/game.h       — GAME_MAX_TICKS=300 headless guard (unchanged from Sprint 8 fix)
tools/to_stf.py     — NEW: universal converter (GGUF, SafeTensors, synthetic)

architecture_decisions.STF_rationale: GGUF/SafeTensors/ONNX are ecosystem formats with external dependencies. Kernel must never change when model formats evolve. STF is the kernel's one rule — host-side converters plug in. Paninian principle: one sutra, unlimited exceptions handled outside.
architecture_decisions.AI_domain_256MiB: Model weights are READ-ONLY firmware at GRUB load address. AI domain holds activations/KV cache/scratch only. 256 MiB covers KV cache for models up to ~7B parameters. Models become swappable without kernel changes.
architecture_decisions.Q8_block_format: STF_Q8_BLOCK_SIZE=32 weights + 2 bytes fp16 scale = 34 bytes/block. Compatible with llama.cpp Q8_0 block layout for direct weight reuse.
